In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) the identification of the range of methods, techniques, and other method fragments used by Web designers in Ireland, (ii) an analysis of the nature of these methods and techniques, (iii) an investigation of the extent to which these methods and techniques are used in practice, and (iv) an examination of the factors that affect their use.

the question: what are the methods and techniques being used in practice by Web/hypermedia designers in Ireland?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods and techniques employed by the Web design community are, in fact, a hybrid of traditional and new approaches.

the designers surveyed have not been “forced” to abandon traditional methods and techniques, and have not been “left to their own devices” in their quest for new and innovative approaches, but rather that they are using and adapting the methods and techniques that they find most appropriate to their context.

the Web/hypermedia design community has not abandoned the use of methods and techniques in favour of a “do it yourself” approach. Rather it seems that a more eclectic approach to method use has been adopted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methods and techniques employed by Web designers are not necessarily new, and are not necessarily specific to the Web.
the Web design process is a complex, multi-faceted, multi-disciplinary and multi-organizational endeavor.
Web/hypermedia system designers in Ireland do not use a single method, but rather a collection of techniques and methods that have been blended together to suit their needs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Web designers in Ireland do not seem to be particularly interested in “new methods” or “new techniques”. Rather, the focus is on the effective application of existing methods and techniques in the context of the Web.
the notion of “Web method” may be more a misnomer than a reality.
, in the Web design context in particular, the notion of the ‘method’ is not a fixed entity.
